decisionMemo.businessProblem: A mid-cap asset-based trucking carrier with ~$800M revenue has seen EBITDA margin fall from 11.0% (FY2024) to 8.0% (FY2025), a 300 bps decline, with the operating ratio deteriorating from 91% to 94% and nearing a lender covenant threshold. Volumes are roughly stable (total miles ~500M, revenue essentially flat at $800M vs $792M), so this is not a demand collapse. Instead, the economics of the marginal mile have broken down: cost per mile is rising fast (fuel +15% to $0.40/mi, driver wages +12% to $0.62/mi) while revenue per mile is falling (down 3.6% to $1.60 from $1.66) in a soft, competitive freight market where the fuel surcharge lags and under-recovers, especially on spot freight. The core challenge before the ~90-day bid season and lender review: is the margin decline a unit-cost-vs-unit-revenue breakdown that can be fixed by shedding unprofitable lanes/customers, re-rating the fuel surcharge, and improving utilization/driver productivity — or is it a broad pricing-strategy problem or a demand-mismatch problem? The carrier must diagnose precisely and act before bid commitments and the covenant test lock in the current trajectory.
